entities.name: Demetrios Laskaris Leontares
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Demetrios Laskaris Leontares (died 15 September 1431), also known as Leontarios, stood as one of the Byzantine Empire's most formidable military commanders and astute diplomats during its twilight years in the early 15th century. Operating amidst the relentless territorial encroachments of the Ottoman Empire and the internal fragmentation of the Palaiologan dynasty, Leontares served as a crucial bulwark for emperors Manuel II Palaiologos and John VIII Palaiologos, embodying the desperate resilience of a collapsing imperium. His career spanned critical engagements that sought to preserve Byzantine sovereignty and cultural heritage against overwhelming odds, primarily centered on Constantinople and the Peloponnese.

Leontares distinguished himself through a series of military and political actions aimed at stabilizing the beleaguered empire. In 1403, he commanded the Byzantine forces that successfully defended Constantinople against an Ottoman siege, a crucial victory that leveraged the chaos of the Ottoman Interregnum. He was instrumental in the defense of the Morea, particularly in the restoration and fortification of the Hexamilion wall across the Isthmus of Corinth in 1415, a monumental engineering effort personally overseen by Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos to protect the Despotate of Morea. His diplomatic missions were equally vital, including an embassy to the Ottoman court in Bursa in 1416 to negotiate peace, and a significant role in the negotiations that led to the marriage of John VIII Palaiologos to Anna of Moscow in 1414, forging a strategic alliance with Muscovy.
